nodes.label: Planning Engineer — Ingest Screen
NAVIS Sidebar Navigation (Home/Reconcile/Schedule/Ingest/Memory)
Project Context Bar (OIL Well-Site Duliajan / OIL-WSD-2026 / Sector A Digboi Well #4)
Drop-file Upload Zone
Accepted File Type Policy (.txt / .xlsx only)
nodes.rationale: Photos, images, PDFs and scanned documents are explicitly refused so that ingestion works on structured, losslessly decodable text rather than OCR guesses; this keeps every extracted event traceable to an exact source line.

nodes.label: Pipeline Trace: PARSED → EXTRACTED → PROPOSED → STAGED
nodes.rationale: Each ingestion stage is shown as a discrete, inspectable step so the planner can see exactly where a file stalled and why — retrieval, extraction and proposal stay visibly separate rather than collapsing into one opaque 'processed' state.

nodes.label: Staged: No Actual Dates Written Before Approval
nodes.rationale: Extraction produces proposals, never direct schedule writes. Staging 15 events without committing any actual date protects the baseline from an unreviewed model output.

nodes.label: Extracted Events Table (Src Ln / Raw Text / Discipline / Tags / Date / Conf. / Outcome)
Three-Way Event Outcome (High-confidence / Sent to review / Flagged unscheduled)
nodes.rationale: A single confidence number is not actionable; splitting outcomes into auto-suggest, human review and unscheduled-work flags routes each event to the cheapest correct handler and keeps out-of-baseline work visible instead of silently dropped.

nodes.label: Source Line Number Provenance (Src Ln column)
Recent Ingest History (files, events, confirmed counts)
Append-Only Audit Retention of Files and Events
nodes.rationale: Every file and extracted event is retained rather than overwritten, so a later correction adds history instead of erasing the earlier claim.

nodes.label: Planning Engineer — Ingest Error States Screen
State: Unsupported File Type
State: Duplicate File Already Ingested
nodes.rationale: Identical content is detected and refused so re-uploading a daily report cannot double-count progress against the same activities.

nodes.label: State: Parsed But Zero Progress Events Found
nodes.rationale: A successful parse with no extractable updates is reported distinctly from a parse failure, so the planner knows the file was read and simply carried nothing.

nodes.label: Uniform Recovery Action: Choose Another File
Responsive Navigation (mobile top bar / desktop side rail)
Planning Engineer — Project Memory Screen
Planned vs Actual Duration Table
Suggested Planning Duration from Confirmed Actuals
nodes.rationale: Suggestions are derived only from confirmed actual durations on this project, not from a global model, so the recommendation is defensible to the planner who approved the underlying data.

nodes.label: Slip by Discipline (Piping/Civil/Electrical/Structural/Instrum./HSE)
Recurring Delay Causes (material shortage, weather, drawing clarification, crane breakdown, permit delay, rework)
Project Memory as Accumulated Learning
nodes.rationale: Framing the screen as 'what this project has learned so far' commits the system to feeding confirmed reconciliation outcomes back into planning, closing the loop between ingest and future baselines.

nodes.label: Planning Engineer — Reconcile Screen
Review Queue (confidence-ranked, priority-tagged report list)
Discipline Filter + 'Only below 60%' Confidence Filter
Source Evidence Pane (file:line with surrounding context)
nodes.rationale: The reviewer is shown the raw line plus the lines around it (FR-2023-10-24.txt : L42) rather than a paraphrase, so the decision is made against the original report and not against the extractor's summary.

nodes.label: Explicit Review Reason (low confidence, multiple potential matches)
nodes.rationale: Stating why an item was routed to review (deterministic reason, not model prose) makes the queue auditable and tells the planner what to check first.

nodes.label: Extracted Entities Panel (Discipline, Equipment/Material, Quantity, Asserted Date, Confidence Score)
Ranked Candidate Baseline Activities (ACT-M-4012, ACT-M-4015)
nodes.rationale: Retrieval offers several candidates with planned dates, discipline and planned quantity so the human ranks them; the system marks one SUGGESTED but never auto-commits it.

nodes.label: Decision Actions: Confirm Match / Reject / Flag as Unscheduled Work
Keyboard-First Queue Operation (J/K navigate, 1–9 select, Enter confirm, U unscheduled, R reject)
nodes.rationale: A planner clearing dozens of reports per session needs throughput; binding every decision to a single key removes the mouse from the critical path.

nodes.label: Confirmation Receipt (alias entries created, audit records appended)
nodes.rationale: The toast reports side effects in system terms ('2 alias entries created · 3 audit records appended') so the reviewer learns that confirming also teaches the matcher a vocabulary alias, not just sets a date.

nodes.label: Alias Learning from Confirmed Matches
Planning Engineer — Reconcile, Save Failure State
Decision Save Failure with Cancel / Retry
nodes.rationale: A failed write is surfaced as an explicit retryable error rather than an optimistic success, because a silently lost confirmation would leave the audit trail disagreeing with what the planner believes they approved.

nodes.label: Planning Engineer — Reconcile, No Candidates State
State: No Matching Baseline Activity Found
nodes.rationale: When retrieval returns nothing the panel says so plainly and leaves 'Flag as Unscheduled Work' available, converting a matcher miss into a captured out-of-baseline record instead of a dead end.

nodes.label: Planning Engineer — Reconcile, Queue Clear State
State: Queue Clear with Session Resolution Count
nodes.rationale: Reporting 'you resolved 30 reports this session' turns an empty list into positive completion feedback and gives the planner a throughput figure for the day.

nodes.label: Empty Detail Pane Prompt
Planning Engineer — Schedule Screen
Schedule Activity Table (Planned/Actual Start & Finish, Start Var, Finish Var, % Comp, Conf)
Baseline Activity Identifiers (CIV-SIT-1001, CIV-FDN-1007, SEQ-PMP-1060)
Schedule Integrity Warnings (source conflicts + date warnings)
nodes.rationale: Conflicts between two sources asserting different actual dates are surfaced as warnings on the schedule rather than resolved silently by last-write-wins, because the schedule is the artifact other teams plan against.

nodes.label: Partial Progress Carries No Actual Finish (50% row shows finish '—')
nodes.rationale: An actual finish date is withheld until an activity is fully complete; recording a finish at partial scope would understate remaining work and corrupt downstream float calculations.

nodes.label: Activity Details Side Panel (dates, predecessors, logic)
Append-Only Audit Trail per Activity (old → new, source, confidence, actor)
nodes.rationale: Each date change records the previous value, the new value, the source document and row, the confidence band, and whether a human or a system extract made it — so any actual date can be defended months later.

nodes.label: Confidence Band Display (High / Med / SYSTEM EXTRACT / Auto-confirmed)
Schedule Export Action
Data Date Anchor (15 Sep 2026, 120 baseline activities)
Technical Precision Design System
nodes.rationale: The visual language is deliberately flat and undecorated — no gradients, no glassmorphism — so site supervisors and project managers reading dense progress data feel stability rather than visual noise.

nodes.label: Industrial Blue / Technical Gray Palette
Functional Constraint: No Green for Complete States
nodes.rationale: Green is reserved by architectural safety standards on site; using it for 'complete' in the UI would collide with that meaning, so completion is carried by Primary Blue or high-contrast grays instead.

nodes.label: Inter Type Scale (display-lg → label-md)
Fixed 12-Column Desktop Grid, 4px Spacing Rhythm
nodes.rationale: 16px gutters are held fixed to maintain high information density appropriate to technical schedule data rather than airy marketing layouts.

nodes.label: Flat Elevation via 1px Outlines, No Drop Shadows
High-Density Data Table Spec (zebra stripe, highlight hover, heading-blue headers)
Component Specification (buttons, inputs, cards, chips, icons, progress bars)
claude-usage Agent Guidance (AGENTS.md)
scanner.py — JSONL Transcript Parser to SQLite
cli.py — Terminal Commands (scan/today/week/stats/dashboard)
dashboard.py — Single-File http.server SPA
SQLite Schema (turns / sessions / processed_files)
nodes.rationale: turns is the source of truth for tokens and per-model attribution; sessions is a denormalized rollup, and processed_files tracks (path, mtime, lines) so an incremental rescan only reads bytes past the last processed line.

nodes.label: Invariant: Streaming Dedupe by message.id
nodes.rationale: Claude Code writes several JSONL records per API response and only the last one for a message.id carries final usage tallies, so parse_jsonl_file keeps the last record per id — summing across records of the same id would multiply token counts.

nodes.label: Invariant: Session Totals Recomputed from turns After Scan
nodes.rationale: upsert_sessions adds additively while insert_turns uses INSERT OR IGNORE, so duplicates would drift session totals; a final UPDATE ... SELECT SUM FROM turns reconciles the two and must survive any refactor of scan().

nodes.label: Invariant: Session Primary Model Priority opus > sonnet > haiku
nodes.rationale: Prevents a subagent's haiku turn from overwriting an opus session's summary model; per-turn model is always honored in turns, the priority only shapes the session-level rollup.

nodes.label: Per-Turn Cost Calculation and Three-Tier Pricing Resolution
nodes.rationale: Costs are computed per turn then summed because each turn knows its own model; aggregating tokens first and applying one price is wrong for multi-model sessions. Unmatched models bill at $0 (shown n/a) on purpose so local or third-party models aren't charged Sonnet rates.

nodes.label: Pricing Duplicated in cli.py PRICING and dashboard.py PRICING (must stay in sync)
Data Flow: JSONL → parse → aggregate → usage.db → CLI / /api/data
Constraint: Stdlib-Only, No pip install, Python 3.8+
nodes.rationale: Anyone running Claude Code already has Python; refusing third-party dependencies keeps install to a clone and removes any build or virtualenv step.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md as Thin @AGENTS.md Import
nodes.rationale: All guidance lives in AGENTS.md so it is shared with Codex and other agents; CLAUDE.md only @-imports it, avoiding two drifting copies of the same rules.

nodes.label: Claude Code Usage Dashboard (product overview)
JSONL Usage Fields (input/output/cache_creation/cache_read tokens, message.model)
Install Paths (Homebrew tap, uv tool/pipx, clone, Docker)
Incremental Scan by Path + Modification Time
Cost Estimates from Published API Pricing
Coverage Boundary: Cowork Sessions Not Captured (no local JSONL)
Claude Code Usage VS Code Extension
nodes.rationale: The extension bundles the Python sources and embeds the same dashboard in a webview iframe rather than reimplementing the UI, so web and editor surfaces cannot diverge.

nodes.label: Interpreter/CLI Discovery Order (setting → bundled → PATH shim → workspace → sibling)
Local-Only Privacy Posture (no API calls, no telemetry)
Subagent Token Attribution View
/triage — Weekly Autonomous Triage Command
nodes.rationale: Designed to run headless on a scheduler, so the command is written as hard rails plus a linear workflow rather than judgment calls an unattended agent cannot make safely.

nodes.label: Triage Hard Safety Rails (dirty-worktree guard, never push main, auto-merge limits)
nodes.rationale: An unattended agent must never destroy staged maintainer work or ship a release, so it aborts on a dirty worktree, refuses git reset --hard entirely, and blocks auto-merge on security keywords, workflow/script edits, dependency additions, deletions, renames and schema changes.

nodes.label: Mechanical Codex Sign-Off Artifact Gate
nodes.rationale: Sign-off is a file that must exist and contain an exact phrase before any close fires — a checkable artifact rather than an advisory opinion, so the gate cannot be rationalized away mid-run.

nodes.label: Green-Baseline-Before-Work Test Gate
Tests Workflow (unittest on Python 3.9/3.11/3.12)
VS Code Extension CI (npm ci, tsc --noEmit, npm test, package .vsix)
Tag-and-Release from CHANGELOG Workflow
nodes.rationale: CHANGELOG.md is the single source of truth; the tag and the GitHub Release are deterministic projections of a newly added '## vX.Y.Z' heading. Full history is fetched so a heading in a non-tip commit is still detected, and two new headings in one push fail loudly rather than shipping an ambiguous release.

nodes.label: claude-usage CHANGELOG (versioned release history)
Change: Est. Cost Overlay Priced Per Model Before Daily Aggregation
Change: Additive In-Place Schema Migration (sessions.topic, is_subagent)
nodes.rationale: New columns are added in place with a one-time backfill flagged in schema_meta so existing databases upgrade without a rebuild and the backfill never repeats; read commands run the same idempotent migration so reading before the next scan cannot crash on a missing column.

nodes.label: DPR Day 01 — 03/08/2026, OIL Well-Site Duliajan
Foundation Concreting Pipe Rack Pedestals P7–P12
Tank TK-1 Shell Erection (course-by-course progress)
24 inch Main Header P-1001 Spool Erection
Crane Breakdown Delay on Tier 2 Steel Erection
Vessel V-101 Separator Arrival
TK-1 Hydrotest Rescheduled 23 Aug → 25 Aug
Back-Dated Completion Claim ("completed yesterday (2 Aug)", "pour completed on 30 Jul")
nodes.rationale: The report date is not the event date — completions are routinely asserted for earlier days, so an extractor that assumes the header date as the actual date will systematically record the wrong actual finish.

nodes.label: DPR Day 02 — 06/08/2026, OIL Well-Site Duliajan
Backfilling Equipment Foundations EF-1/EF-2/EF-3 Completed
Containment Bund Wall Zone A Rebar Fixing (65%)
V-101 Separator Jacking (lift-count progress)
Level / Pressure Transmitter Calibration in Workshop
Field Noise: Misspellings and Informal Phrasing ("Crain operator", "equip foundation")
nodes.rationale: Real reports carry typos and abbreviations, so matching cannot rely on exact string equality against baseline activity names.

nodes.label: DPR Day 03 — 11/08/2026, OIL Well-Site Duliajan
P-1001 Spool Erection Complete (all 18 spools)
Pipe Support Installation Tier 1 (98 of 145)
HT Cable Laying 33kV Substation → MCC Trench
MCC Panel Installation and Transformer TR-01 Oil Filling
Junction Boxes JB-01/JB-02/JB-03 Installed and Tagged
Code-Mixed Hinglish Progress Line ("tiles ka kaam chalu hai")
nodes.rationale: Site engineers write in mixed Hindi-English; the extractor must still recover the quantity (40 m2 of 95 m2) from a line whose verb phrase is not English.

nodes.label: Forward-Looking Plan Statements ("planned 13 Aug", "expected by 15 Aug")
nodes.rationale: Future intentions sit in the same bullet list as completed work; treating them as actuals would write finish dates for work that has not happened.

nodes.label: DPR Data Shape (header metadata, numbered discipline sections, lettered/bulleted activity lines, REMARKS)
nodes.rationale: Every DPR carries a date/weather/contractor/preparer header, then discipline-numbered sections (CIVIL, PIPING, EQUIPMENT, ELECTRICAL, INSTRUMENTATION, HSE, MATERIALS) whose lines mix quantity, percent-complete, tag identifiers and free narrative — the shape the extractor must key on, even though section numbering and bullet style vary between days.

nodes.label: Quantity-Based Progress Idiom (X of Y done, N%, m3 / MT / lm / m2 units)
Equipment / Line Tag Identifiers (P-1001, V-101, E-101, TK-1, EF-2, CS-01, TR-01, JB-01)
nodes.rationale: Tag codes are the most reliable join key between a free-text report line and a baseline activity, far more stable than the surrounding prose.
